On 15 Jun 2016, at 13:39, Michael Kunst wrote:

> I ust wanted again to say how great it was meeting you, it really
> helped me a lot in thinking about the future of my project. I also
> delved a bit more into the nat package. I already figured out how to
> rescale the dimension of my tracing and how to apply my registration
> to my tracings as well.

Super!

> I’m currently in the process of generating a template brain and
> wanted to know what you used to make the associated .surf file. I
> assume it was Amira.

Yes

> We do not have an Amira license, can I just use FluoRender or ImageJ
> to generate this file?

I believe that you can do this in both programs, although I have not
tried. With ImageJ google offered this:

http://132.187.25.13/ij3d/?category=Extensions&page=Create_Surfaces

The plugin mentioned may already be included in Fiji. There is also a
tool called ITK SNAP used a lot in human brain imaging that should be
good.

We have ways write now to import amira hxurf, obj or ply format into R.
I can provide specific details depending on what output format you end
up with. Meshlab is a useful software for looking at / editing /
converting surface meshes.

Best,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: problems with reformatting a swc
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,

I would say that you want the reference brain and the template brain to
be in the same physical space. Are the voxdims "wrong" on one of these
brains?

The registrations all include an explicit notion of space. Therefore it
would be better if the templates had the same calibration. But you will
need to re-run the registrations you already have if the template brain
calibration changes.

If you just need to recalibrate the neurons before transformation, you
can do:

myneurons.fixed=myneurons*voxdims("template.nrrd")

This will work for neuronlists (containing multiple neurons) and also
for individual neurons. See also ?scale.neuron.

A couple of other notes. The resample function will resample along a
traced neuron to change the stepsize between the points in the
reconstruction. nrrd.voxdims is a specialised function and in general I
would use voxdims since that should work for any supported image type.

All the best,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: problems with reformatting a swc
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,

On 29 Jun 2016, at 9:25, Michael Kunst wrote:

> So I think I figured out what the main problem is, and it seems that
> the software I’m using to visualize the data is not able to take the
> image resolution into account, so it always assumes that the voxels
> are isotropic and (1,1,1).

Which software is that? I guess one get SWCs into Fiji and that has
basic 3D visualisation. We have also used paraview (there is a vtk
export function in the development version of nat).

> So the only reason why I even got images that looked somewhat good is
> that my resolution ended up being 0.9271, 09271, 1.

I see.

> I guess I should figure out a way to generate the surface file and use
> the nat package to visualize my neurons in a standard brain. I finally
> got access to a Computer with AMIRA, so that should happen soon.

OK, I think you might find that useful. In Amira, I recommend
resampling/smoothing your starting image to around 2um isotropic voxels,
constructing a surface using an appropriate threshold and then
simplifying that down to somewhere between 15,000 - 30,000 polygons (I
did all of mine at 18,000).

> However, I will still have problem because the voxdim function return
> the “wrong” dimension. When I look at the image properties in Fiji
> the resolution of the template and the reference brain are the same,
> so I’m not quite sure why the voxdim values are different. I guess
> since I know the specific value I can just adjust them manually.

Are your templates both nrrd files? You can inspect the complete header
of the file using

nat::read.nrrd.header

or from the unu command line suite (http://teem.sourceforge.net/unrrdu/
very useful if you don't have it) using

unu head

> Another question. My current workflow is that I calibrate my swc
> before using xform to the resolution of the original image (which is
> generally higher). Are you saying it would make more sense to
> calibrate it to the resolution of the template?

If your tracing software does not save the tracings with spatial
calibration, you need to calibrate the swcs according to match the image
that they were traced from.

Best,

Greg.
